answer: Stop sybils with a pearl bond, a haven sponsor, and a dune audit. Each identity locks one pearl, a bond receipt chained to its funder and haven, and a haven sponsors only one newcomer per epoch. Standing needs stakes from unrelated members. A dune audit reshuffles auditors every epoch, so clones cannot predict cover. When audits trace several identities to one funder or one haven, they collapse into one standing and every linked pearl is slashed, multiplied by the collapsed count. One agent risks one pearl; N copies stake N pearl bonds for one standing and forfeit roughly N squared.
